Director seat, summon #25, `session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`. Presented in detail with the recommendation **A**; the maintainer agreed 「其他同意」. Thread re-read to its last comment (5707798018) in the act that wrote this. Facts (card measurement on `origin/main` `3faaa7d0f`, triage-verified anchors): CONTROL `properties.label: "L-${record.id}"` renders `L-rec_1`; CASE A node-level `params.recordId: "${record.id}"` and CASE B `properties.params.recordId` both reach the handler **raw**; `DeclaredActionsBar.tsx:110` injects the row and `action:button` does not; `recordFormNavigation.ts:286-287` has no context fallback for `recordId` by design; `action-button.tsx:150-219` forwards a whitelist without `recordId` / `objectName`.

## Ruling — **A**: an action's `params` values are templates

Every **string leaf** of an action's `params` bag — the node-level `params` and `properties.params` alike, at any depth — is template-evaluated in the **same memo** that already evaluates `properties`, on every surface that renders `action:button`. One rule, stated once: *params values are templates, evaluated where `properties` are.* ⛔ **B refused** (row injection overturns a difference `DeclaredActionsBar` records as deliberate); ⛔ **C refused** (a context leg in one resolver, against its own docblock, fixes one handler); ⛔ **D refused** (a metadata-authored button that cannot name the record it sits on is the 「declared, not honoured」 shape this project ends, not documents).

Behaviour change reaches only authors whose templates never worked (they received the raw `${…}` text and a wrong URL); anything left unresolved keeps hitting the unevaluated-expression diagnostic, so a wrong template stays loud. The claiming seat carries the depth-1 qualification to objectui#7849 as a comment (its 「`properties` works」 held only at depth 1 until this lands), and the doc note PR #7865 added to `content/docs/guide/record-edit-modes.md` returns to teaching `"recordId": "${record.id}"` in the same PR.

Four-facet reading (this seat's own): ① declarative buttons whose parameters resolve against the current record are the industry shape (Salesforce custom-button URL merge fields, ServiceNow UI actions reading `current`); one rule beats three doors each opened a crack; ② a published guide taught this spelling and every author writing a per-row edit button hits it; ③ writable, schema-valid, silently inert today — the class-(c) shape; after A it resolves or reports; ④ zero new concepts, no special case.

`Prior rulings read:` objectui#7849 (the depth qualification lands there), objectui#7440 / PR #7865 (the doc half), thread: 1.

## Execution, same stroke

`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` stand. `Clause-②: yes` (published renderer behaviour changes); changeset `minor`. Pins: CASE A and CASE B resolve to `rec_1`, a nested template two levels down resolves, CONTROL unchanged, an unresolvable template still reports.

### The dev's open question: reading 1, `Fixes` stands

The ruling states its rule once: 「params values are templates, evaluated where `properties` are」. It sites the evaluation in 「the same memo」 and refuses a second evaluator. `action:bar` / `action:group` / `action:menu` members mount through the component registry, so their `properties` are not evaluated either. That is a separate, pre-existing gap, not a remainder of this ruling. It is filed as its own card, per the dev's recommendation B.

### Out of scope

- **class a**: the shallow `properties` loop collapses any object value carrying a string `source` key, because the evaluator unwraps it as an expression envelope. `params` no longer does. ⇒ filed by the seat after dedupe.
- **class b**: `UIActionSchema.params` and spec `ActionSchema.params` are `ActionParam[]`-only, the object form is refused by name, and spec `PageComponentSchema` declares no node-level `params`. Yet the runtime, `AppContent`'s `navigate_create` / `navigate_edit` and the guide use an object bag. ⇒ filed by the seat after dedupe; the contract half is `domain:spec`'s.
- **Acceptance notes**: `check-doc-expression-carriage`'s hit text still says 「exactly four channels」. The census reads only top-level strings, so it neither counts nor misjudges `params`. Report-only; noted, not filed.
- **Acceptance notes**: the guide's 「is not an error」 for a misspelled field on a bound record is imprecise. `navigate_edit` returns its own required-id error. Non-blocking.

The seat carries the depth-1 qualification to objectui#7849, as the ruling asks, in a separate comment.
